name: Dalton's shed

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 707-715); when it was built is not known, and the scene's phase begins in 1860.

change_note: Built T-3689 (2026-11-20): the O'Leary site on DeKoven Street, on the landmark_1871 archetype in the 1835 town's clapboard and shingles.

placement.position_note: At the rear of Dalton's lot on its west line (Andreas vol. 2, p. 712), beside the O'Leary barn. The footprint's origin is local E -315.15 N -1930.03.
placement.symbolic_location: At the rear of 135 DeKoven Street, on the north alley.

blocks.name: Dalton's shed
blocks.note: A shed twelve by twenty feet at the rear of Dalton's lot on its west line, joined to his house by an eight-foot fence (Andreas vol. 2, p. 712); its roof and door are reconstructed.

fire.note: Beside the barn: the high fences that ran from the barn to the sheds on the next lots carried the fire to them at once (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708).

value.note: DALTON'S SHED, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: a board shed twelve by twenty feet at the rear of 135 DeKoven Street, beside the O'Leary barn (Andreas vol. 2, p. 712). The high wooden fences that ran from the barn to the sheds on the next lots carried the fire to them.

composition.note: Sizes from Andreas's account where he gives them; storeys, roofs and openings from the photograph where it shows them, else reconstructed as the neighbourhood's one-storey frame cottages.

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 2, From 1857 until the Fire of 1871. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885.
